paths.description: Entry dashboard, global navigation, market summary and mixed editorial feed. Represents shared chrome and the highest-density landing template.
TSMC quote detail, chart and related-news template. Represents the primary stock-research journey.
Market category/index template with dense quote links.
Stock-screening journey for a signed-out user, including the login boundary and predefined strategies.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot remains the same white interface as the default capture, and the live CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme, light-dark(), or color-scheme implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface, text, border, chart, and advertisement-container tokens.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences receive no dedicated treatment.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more capture does not materially change controls or text, the CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules, and Lighthouse reports color-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations, preserve system colors and visible control boundaries, and retest charts and icon-only controls.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The cross-template CSS probe found no view-transition rules or API styling on home, quote, listing, news, or screener surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route and meaningful state changes with same-document or cross-document View Transitions while retaining instant fallback behavior.

findings.summary: The long landing page gives no scroll-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The 6,617px desktop landing capture has static chrome and no progress cue; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or scroll-timeline implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a restrained shrinking header or progress indicator driven by scroll-state/container queries where it helps orientation.

findings.summary: Advertising and auxiliary chrome compete with financial content.
findings.evidence: The home and screener captures show multiple large banners, a right-rail ad, native-ad rows interleaved with news, and repeated navigation/search bars before core content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve fewer, clearly separated ad slots, defer below-fold ad systems, and reduce duplicated navigation so market data and task controls dominate each viewport.

findings.summary: The requested mobile viewport renders a scaled 1,020px desktop canvas.
findings.evidence: All five 360x800 layout captures report clientWidth 1,020 and hasViewportMeta false; screenshots are desktop layouts shrunk to roughly 35%, making text and controls extremely small.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid width=device-width viewport declaration without disabling zoom, then rebuild shared chrome, tables, cards and ad slots as mobile-first fluid layouts.

findings.summary: Reusable components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: CSS probes across all five templates found no @container rules; dense cards and tables retain desktop arrangements in the scaled mobile canvas.
findings.suggestedFix: Define inline-size containers around shared cards/tables and use container queries to stack, abbreviate, or disclose secondary data at narrow component widths.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The custom probe found 50 visible controls under 24px on the home page, and Lighthouse failed target-size; this is amplified by the 0.35 mobile scale.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt at least 44x44 CSS-pixel touch areas or equivalent spacing, preserve visible :focus-visible rings, and avoid icon-only links without larger hit areas.

findings.summary: Primary templates miss the performance and stability baseline.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured home LCP 8.5s, TBT 610ms and performance 0.44; screener measured LCP 4.6s, CLS 0.289, TBT 580ms and performance 0.38.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce initial third-party/script work, reserve dynamic regions, and break or defer tasks before re-measuring on representative devices.

findings.summary: The screener and image markup allow visible layout movement.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.289 on screener; the image inventory found 25 of 30 home images without width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic image/ad/card space with width, height or aspect-ratio and diagnose the screener CLS culprits before late content is inserted.

findings.summary: JavaScript blocks responsiveness during load.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded three long tasks, longest 196ms and TBT 184ms under a warm local capture; Lighthouse under throttling measured 610ms TBT and 27.7s to interactive.
findings.suggestedFix: Use code coverage to remove unused startup code, split work into scheduler-yielding tasks, and delay analytics/ad work until after core market UI is interactive.

findings.summary: The critical load is dominated by scripts and third parties.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 222 requests and 3.57MB transferred, including 2.50MB script and 3.42MB classified third-party; it also identified eight first-party parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets before third-party styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, audit preload priorities, and gate ad/analytics bundles behind consent and post-interaction loading.

findings.summary: Large advertising and analytics bundles dominate shipped code.
findings.evidence: HAR largest scripts include Taboola 217KB, Google Publisher 200KB, Prebid 184KB and GTM 166KB; Lighthouse also reports missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant vendors, load revenue code only in slots that become viewable, and use coverage/bundle analysis to split unused first-party modules.

findings.summary: Important controls and content lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails link-name and label-content-name-mismatch; the image inventory reports 20 of 30 images without alt, and 85 of 294 home links have no discernible text in the DOM probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable icon/link a programmatic name matching visible text, label search fields, and provide meaningful or empty alt according to image purpose.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit fails on both home and screener, corroborated by the unchanged high-contrast preference capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust semantic color tokens to WCAG minimum ratios in every state and verify market gain/loss colors with non-color cues.

findings.summary: Pages have no main landmark and contain noisy heading/link structure.
findings.evidence: All five DOM probes report zero main landmarks; Lighthouse fails landmark-one-main and link-name, while quote has two h1 elements and screener uses another h1 for the login state.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap unique page content in one main landmark, keep one descriptive h1, repair heading order, and remove unnamed focus stops.

findings.summary: Viewport policy prevents normal zoom and reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails meta-viewport because user-scalable=no or maximum-scale below 5 is present; CDP mobile layouts report hasViewportMeta false and a 1,020px layout scaled to 360px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 without maximum-scale or user-scalable restrictions, then test 200% zoom, 320px reflow and touch target spacing.

findings.summary: The page emits browser errors during normal load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails errors-in-console on both home and screener; the HAR also records failed consent/cookie-sync requests and aborted analytics/ad requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix uncaught/runtime errors, handle optional vendor failures without console noise, and add production monitoring keyed to first-party exceptions.

findings.summary: Asset markup is not consistently sound.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 25/30 images without intrinsic dimensions, four oversized images and six legacy-format assets; Lighthouse reports low-resolution image delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions and responsive srcset/sizes, choose appropriate modern formats, and avoid low-resolution placeholders as final rendered assets.

findings.summary: The page has several platform-hygiene failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports deprecated API usage, missing source maps, inspector issues and a BFCache failure on both tested templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated calls, publish usable source maps privately or publicly as policy allows, resolve DevTools issues, and eliminate avoidable unload/BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Some navigation is unnamed or not crawlable, and mobile metadata is harmful.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails crawlable-anchors and meta-viewport; the probe counts 85 empty-name links on home and 77 on screener.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href links with descriptive accessible text, repair icon-only anchors, and publish a zoom-safe responsive viewport declaration.

findings.summary: The CSP provides framing control but little script/style XSS defense.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but Content-Security-Policy contains only frame-ancestors and does not constrain script-src, style-src, object-src or base-uri.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP in report-only mode, inventory required origins, then enforce tight script/style/default/object/base directives.

findings.summary: The default load has a very large tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 25 third-party origins and 11 known tracker domains; HAR classified 217/222 requests and 3.42MB/3.57MB as third-party, including Google, Taboola and PubMatic systems.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors, require purpose-specific consent before non-essential tracking, batch analytics, shorten retention and provide an equally usable reject path.

findings.summary: Browser defense headers are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The header audit found no Permissions-Policy and only a legacy no-referrer-when-downgrade Referrer-Policy; framing is covered by CSP frame-ancestors and HSTS is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, use strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer handling, and evaluate Trusted Types/origin isolation for this script-heavy app.

findings.summary: Core dashboard, quote and news content is largely absent without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability comparisons found only 25% raw/rendered word coverage on home, 16% on the TSMC quote and 31% on news, although titles and h1 survive.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core prices, headings, article links and summaries, then hydrate enhancements so no-JS and constrained clients receive the primary information.

findings.summary: Unknown routes depend on script or meta refresh and lose site context.
findings.evidence: A missing stock route correctly returns HTTP 404, but its body only redirects with JavaScript or noscript meta refresh to the general Yahoo homepage error surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an in-context stock-site 404 with search, recent route recovery and a real link fallback, without requiring script to understand or recover.

findings.summary: The document language is correct but layout CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: All probes report lang=zh-Hant-TW, but no logical properties were detected and dozens of physical left/right declarations were present on home, quote and news.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the correct language metadata and migrate reusable spacing/position rules to inline/block logical properties.

findings.summary: Native-looking advertisements are interleaved with editorial results.
findings.evidence: The home feed screenshot includes rows such as “Search For Booking Software” and “Find Results…” styled like news cards with only a small Ad label, alongside multiple high-prominence banners.
findings.suggestedFix: Visually separate paid placements, use persistent prominent ad labels, and ensure ads cannot be mistaken for finance reporting or primary controls.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and lacks intrinsic metadata.
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 25 images without dimensions, four oversized, six legacy-format, two without srcset and no images recognized as modern format.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive modern-format variants, declare srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions, and verify actual rendered resolution at each container width.

findings.summary: Non-core background and advertising work is substantial.
findings.evidence: The load makes 222 requests, executes 61 scripts, and records repeated analytics/ad calls plus long tasks after content begins rendering.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize or cancel background fetches when hidden, batch analytics, and avoid loading bidder/ad code for slots unlikely to enter the viewport.

findings.summary: Third-party cost is disproportionate to the core finance experience.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 3.42MB of 3.57MB and 217 of 222 requests to third-party origins; the largest non-core scripts include Taboola, Google Publisher, Prebid and GTM.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, lazy-load below-fold ad slots, remove duplicate bidders and measure revenue value against transferred and CPU cost.

findings.summary: The public finance site is deliberately unavailable to major AI agents and exposes no structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: robots.txt disallows anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot and many peers; probes found no WebMCP/agentic capability, while no-JS quote coverage is only 16%.
findings.suggestedFix: Define an explicit agent policy; if safe access is intended, expose read-only structured quote/search tools with scoped schemas and allow appropriate crawlers instead of requiring screen scraping.

findings.summary: Repeated search/scroll interaction retains substantial additional memory.
findings.evidence: Across baseline and post snapshots, heap self-size rose from 53.5MB to 62.9MB and snapshot nodes from 881,921 to 1,036,618; same-session performance.memory rose from 54.8MB to 69.6MB and DOM nodes from 2,177 to 2,863. Lazy feed loading may explain part of this, so leak confidence is medium.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat a controlled open/close or search/reset cycle with forced GC and baseline/target/final snapshots, then remove retained listeners, detached trees or unbounded feed caches identified by retaining paths.
